hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED BASELINE (economics, not an edge test). D1 model (agents/daily/w1-prop/prop_model.py) re-implemented in agents/daily/w3-volrisk/stress_model.py; with no stress it reproduces D1 bit for bit (unit test). Firms: FTMO Swing 2-Step 100K, Blue Guardian 2-Step 100K, CFT 2-Phase 100K with D1's firms.py parameters. Each (firm, S) job simulates D1's full sigma grid {1..40}%/yr once (n=3000 paths, eval seed 11, funded seed 12; common random numbers across S and caps) and reads each vol cap c in {12,15,20,30,40(=no cap)}% as the best (sigma_e, sigma_f) pair with both <= c. Metric: pre-tax net $ per slot-year (renewal reward, as D1 and the synthesis table). S in {0,0.25,...,3.5}. Required Sharpe for $20k per slot-year = linear interpolation on that S grid, per firm and cap.
notes: RESULT: reproduces D1 within noise. $20k needs S 2.42 (12%) / 1.88 (15%) / 1.42 (20%) / 0.96 (30%) / 0.69 (40%) at FTMO; S=0 uncapped FTMO $10.8k.

hypothesis: STRESS: fat tails. Every shock Student-t with 3 degrees of freedom scaled to unit variance (D1: t5). All else F2-01, S in {0,1,1.5,2}.
notes: RESULT: t3 tails cost 1-5% at S>=1 (cap 20%), 5-13% at S=0.

hypothesis: STRESS: gaps. Each trading day 25% of its variance arrives as one jump at the open before any equity check (overnight gap); every 5th trading day (Monday) the opening jump carries one extra day of variance (weekend gap); all variances scaled by 5/6 so annual vol stays sigma. Applied to all three firms (conservative for CFT, whose crypto trades on weekends). The bot has a kill switch: at 80% of the daily loss limit it closes everything and stays flat until the next day, so only a jump can carry it through the limit. Shocks t5. S in {0,1,1.5,2}.
notes: RESULT: gaps with kill switch: 0% FTMO/CFT, +6% BG at cap 20% S=1.5 (kill switch gains offset gap losses).

hypothesis: CONTROL for F2-03: kill switch at 80% of the daily loss limit, no gaps. Separates what the kill switch saves from what gaps cost.
notes: RESULT: kill switch alone +0-8% at cap 20%; up to +19% BG uncapped.

hypothesis: STRESS: volatility clustering. Daily variance multiplier h' = 0.02 + 0.10 z^2 + 0.88 h (GARCH(1,1)-like, persistence 0.98, E[h]=1), z = the day's book move in unconditional daily s.d., h capped at 16 (vol x4). Drift per day unchanged. t5. S in {0,1,1.5,2}.
notes: RESULT: clustering -2 to -6% at S>=1, -25% at S=0 (cap 20%).

hypothesis: STRESS: hard daily loss on equity including floating P&L, strictest convention. Reference = the HIGHER of start-of-day equity and start-of-day closed balance; closed balance lags equity, realising 10% of open P&L per day (daily-rebalanced book), and is set to equity when the bot flattens or takes a payout; equity checked against reference minus limit 24 times a day (D1: 4). Applied to all three firms. t5. S in {0,1,1.5,2}.
notes: RESULT: strictest equity DLL: -18% FTMO, -35% BG, -16% CFT at cap 20% S=1.5; -60% at S=0 uncapped.

hypothesis: FIRM-EXACT rules from the firms' own pages (clauses-*.md, read 2026-10-12, before any F2 run), no market stress: FTMO 5% daily loss from the closed balance at 00:00 CE(S)T checked on equity (floating P&L counts), fee 510 refunded with the first reward; Blue Guardian funded daily loss 4% from the higher of balance or equity (D1 had a 2% hard proxy) plus the Guardian Shield = total open P&L <= -2% of start closes all trades, first trigger cuts the split to 50% (x0.97 processing fee) for the account's life, second breaches; refund 347 after the 4th payout; CFT fee $660 never refunded, 5% daily loss from the start-of-day balance, $10k profit cap per day per user = $3,333 per account in a 3-account fleet (excess cut). Where the reference is balance, closed balance lags equity at 10%/day as F2-06. S in {0,1,1.5,2}.
notes: RESULT: firm-exact: -16% FTMO, -25% BG, -36% CFT at cap 20% S=1.5; CFT -56% uncapped ($10k/user day cap, no refund). BG Shield fires ~2x per funded life even at 12%.

hypothesis: Blue Guardian only: F2-07 with a book that closes and reopens every position each day (all open P&L realised daily), the best case for the Guardian Shield. Trading cost of the daily round trip NOT modelled (optimistic).
notes: RESULT: BG daily-realised book within +-4% of D1 baseline at cap 20%.

hypothesis: DECIDES. Combined: t3 + gaps and kill switch (F2-03) + clustering (F2-05) + 24 checks a day, balance lag 10%/day (F2-06) + firm-exact rules (F2-07; the daily-loss reference is the firm's own, not the F2-06 envelope). S in {0,0.25,...,3.5}; required Sharpe for $20k per slot-year by linear interpolation per firm and cap. Max safe vol per firm = the largest cap c in {12,15,20,30}% such that (a) no clause is breached at c and the clause reader does not rate c high-risk, and (b) under F2-09 at S=1.0 net $/slot-yr at c exceeds that at the next lower cap by more than $250 (about 2 Monte Carlo s.e.); breach-before-first-payout share reported alongside.
notes: RESULT (superseded by F2-12 for the verdict): $20k needs FTMO 2.42/1.92/1.46/0.94 at 12/15/20/30%; CFT 2.52/2.06/1.70/1.47; BG 3.10/2.76/2.46/1.98. Rule (a) clauses: FTMO and CFT pass to 20%, fail 30%; BG fails all. Rule (b) passes every step. Max safe vol 20% FTMO, CFT; none BG.

hypothesis: REAL FEE AND REFUND TIMING: the calendar-order chain (D1 slot_years, 2000 slots x 3 years) under F2-07 rules: every evaluation fee paid when bought, the refund paid on the date of the refund payout (FTMO 1st, Blue Guardian 4th, CFT never). Reports year-1 mean, p10 and P(loss) and years-2-3 mean, p10, p50 per slot, at S in {0,1,1.5,2} and caps 12, 20, 40% (sigma pair from F2-07).
notes: RESULT: FTMO S=1.5 cap 20%: year-1 $12.5k (P loss 18%), yrs 2-3 $17.8k; S=0 cap 20%: yrs 2-3 median $2.2k.

hypothesis: LOTTERY CHECK: as F2-10 under F2-09 (all stresses). The Sharpe-0 'lottery' survives only if, under F2-09, S=0 at the uncapped optimum gives positive net $/slot-yr in renewal reward AND a positive years-2-3 median per slot in the calendar chain.
notes: RESULT: lottery survives under the pre-registered test at FTMO ($9.1k, median $7.2k) and BG ($3.1k/$2.5k) at 40% vol; CFT $1.8k/$1.1k (survives). At cap 20% FTMO S=0 = $2.9k, median $1.3k.

hypothesis: POST-HOC (added after the model red team, agents/daily/w3-volrisk/redteam-model.md, and committed before being run). Corrected F2-09: (i) each day's move is exactly Student-t(3) with a Brownian intraday path given that day's variance (in F2-09 a day was a sum of 24 t3 shocks, close to Gaussian, which undid the fat tails); (ii) GARCH cap raised to h<=100 so E[h]=1 holds; (iii) after a payout the daily-loss reference is recomputed from the post-payout balance; (iv) Blue Guardian bot stop: close everything for the day when open P&L <= -1.6% of start (below the -2% Guardian Shield). Closed balance still realises 10% of open P&L a day. S in {0,0.25,...,3.5}. This row REPLACES F2-09 as the decision row for the verdict; F2-09 is reported next to it.
notes: RESULT (DECIDES): $20k needs FTMO 2.44/1.96/1.46/1.00/0.70 at 12/15/20/30/40%; CFT 2.54/2.09/1.66/1.35/1.29; BG 2.60/2.18/1.76/1.36/1.09 (upper bound; contract fails). FTMO net at cap 20% S=1.5 $20.6k (D1 $21.1k). Max safe vol: 20% FTMO and CFT (rule a), none for BG.

hypothesis: POST-HOC. F2-12 with a book that realises all open P&L every day (close and reopen, real_rate 1), and pays for it: Sharpe reduced by 0.47 (gross notional about 12.5 x annual vol, 1.5 bp round trip a day, 252 days: 252*12.5*1.5e-4 = 0.47 per unit of vol). The verdict uses, per firm, cap and S, the better of F2-12 and F2-13 (the bot can choose how it holds positions).
notes: RESULT: worse than F2-12 in every firm/cap/S cell (e.g. FTMO S=1.5 cap 20% $13.7k), so never decides.

hypothesis: POST-HOC. Calendar chains (as F2-10) under F2-12 and F2-13 at S in {0,1,1.5,2}, caps 12, 20, 40%. Lottery verdict as F2-11 on the better of the two.
notes: RESULT: F2-12 chain FTMO S=1.5 cap 20% year-1 $11.4k, yrs 2-3 $22.0k (p10 $11.6k); S=0: cap 20% median $0.2k (P loss 46%), cap 40% $6.6k median $4.8k. Lottery survives (pre-registered test) at FTMO and BG only at 40% vol; fails at CFT.

hypothesis: POST-HOC. Four more seed pairs of F2-12 at S = 1.0 (eval seeds 101, 202, 303, 404; funded seed +1) to measure the Monte Carlo s.e. of net $/slot-yr and of each cap-to-cap gain.
